prompt: Roadmap III, Prompt 245, One spectral energy distribution on the existing workspace (tranche T4 by D-R10-232-01), the kernel, contract and gate part
document: SED.md (the kernel, conventions and the validation table) and SED_GATE.md (the contract, the gate and the files requested), both written after this file
committed: before js/kernels/sed/*, the validator, the oracle scripts and their pinned results, the synthetic generator's output, any catalogue file, any lesson, and before any flux, magnitude, temperature, luminosity or oracle output of Prompt 245 existed. Phase 1 of the session (reading the roadmap, the register, checkpoint IV, the radiation kernel and its bandpass pack, the statistics kernel and the X-ray, radio and multi-messenger patterns) preceded it and fixed nothing here from a result. No expected value below is the output of the kernel: every one is a closed form (the AB zero point of the radiation kernel's constants, the f_nu / f_lambda relation, the integral of a power law over a box band), arithmetic written in the leg, or a bound set by a stated discretisation (a 1200-node log-temperature grid with cubic interpolation, a 1 nm band refinement, power-law chords between points) or by the Monte Carlo error of a stated ensemble size.
rule: A crossed bound is a failed check, recorded in failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. A leg that cannot be measured (a file not supplied) is NOT RUN and says why. No published flux, magnitude, zero point, filter curve, effective wavelength, catalogue value, distance, temperature, licence term or citation detail is typed anywhere from memory: every authentic fact comes either from a pack already in the tree under its recorded source (the radiation bandpass pack and its AB-Vega offsets, the SDSS stellar spectra pack) or from a file Carl supplied under tests/fixtures/sed/authentic/ with its source, its terms as read from a saved copy and its retrieval date in that directory's SOURCES.json; a product that was not retrieved is rights basis C and nothing of it ships. Every point carries its band, its convention (AB magnitude, Vega magnitude, or a flux-density unit of the registry), whether it is band-integrated or monochromatic, its epoch or the statement that none is known; a point whose convention is unknown, or whose band has no response in the pack, is refused and never guessed. The wavelength of a band-integrated point is its pivot wavelength computed from the response; a monochromatic point states its own wavelength. A blackbody is never evaluated outside the wavelength range of the points that fixed it without the label extrapolated. Synthetic data is labelled and carries its truth manifest.

seeds.design: sed-245-design (used only to build and debug; never in a leg): seed 245000
seeds.note: A stream is stream('noise', seed, label, r) of js/random/streams.js for realisation r; the normals are the Box-Muller of the same module. Each leg names its seed and label below.

scope.built: (1) the point contract and the flux-density conventions: AB and Vega magnitudes per band through the radiation kernel's AB zero point and the pack's AB-Vega offsets, the registry flux units (Jy, mJy, W/m2/nm, erg/s/cm2/Angstrom), f_lambda and f_nu and nu f_nu and lambda f_lambda, and the band-integrated (photon-weighted, Bessell and Murphy 2012) versus monochromatic distinction carried on every point, with every refusal by code; (2) a blackbody fit of temperature and angular radius to an SED, in log flux with the scale profiled out exactly, the temperature interval by profile of chi-square through the statistics kernel's profileInterval, the 2 x 2 covariance, the adequacy test, the fit's wavelength range stated and the model labelled extrapolated outside it; (3) nonsimultaneity as a per-point flag (epoch more than a window from a stated reference, or no epoch) that widens the point's log-flux uncertainty in quadrature by a stated allowance; (4) the integrated flux of the SED between its first and last points by power-law chords, the model's tails below and above them labelled as extrapolation, and the bolometric luminosity with a distance, with an interval by a seeded parametric bootstrap; (5) a labelled synthetic generator with a truth manifest. NOT built: any catalogue pack for a star (rights basis C, nothing retrieved), the SED view, the investigation, the model-page section, instructor materials and Spanish strings; the registry is not extended (see the contract).

synthetic.label: SYNTHETIC SED: generated by js/kernels/sed/synthetic.js from the stated blackbody parameters and seed; the magnitudes and fluxes are the kernel's own blackbody model through the in-tree bandpasses plus Gaussian noise, the four mid-infrared wavelengths are invented reference wavelengths of no instrument, and no star, survey, catalogue or archive is represented.

optical-nir.what: seven band-integrated points on Vega magnitudes: the Johnson-Cousins B V R I of the bandpass pack and the 2MASS J H Ks of the pack

sdss-2mass.what: eight band-integrated points on two conventions at once: SDSS u g r i z on AB magnitudes and 2MASS J H Ks on Vega magnitudes

mir-extra.what: four monochromatic points in Jy with a 3 percent flux error, at invented reference wavelengths of 3400, 4600, 12000 and 22000 nm, appended to sdss-2mass as 'with-mir' (twelve points, three kinds of convention)

rayleigh-jeans.what: four monochromatic points in Jy with a 5 percent flux error at invented reference wavelengths of 12000, 22000, 60000 and 100000 nm: the Rayleigh-Jeans side only

epochs.what: scene 'nonsimultaneous': the points listed carry an epoch 400 days from the reference (the others the reference epoch); the truth moves each of them by an independent factor exp(0.1 e), e standard normal, which is the rule's assumption (independent, zero-mean, equal to the allowance) and not a statement about any star

excess.what: scene 'excess': a second blackbody of 1200 K whose f_nu at 12000 nm is 3 times the star's, added in f_nu before the points are made; the fit is a single blackbody

domain.interpolation: 4-point Lagrange in ln T on a uniform grid (error below 1e-8 of ln flux)

fields.id: a string, unique in the SED
fields.kind: 'band-integrated' (the photon-weighted mean f_nu through a band of the pack: the value of a magnitude or of a flux density 'in the band') or 'monochromatic' (the flux density at one wavelength); no default
fields.band: the id of a band of the bandpass pack (required when band-integrated)
fields.lambdaNm: the wavelength of a monochromatic point, nm (required when monochromatic); a band-integrated point's wavelength is its pivot wavelength from the response, never typed
fields.convention: 'ab-mag', 'vega-mag' or a registry flux unit id ('Jy', 'mJy', 'W/m2/nm', 'erg/s/cm2/Angstrom'); no default; anything else is refused 'convention-unknown'
fields.value, sigma: in the unit of the convention (mag for magnitudes, the flux unit for fluxes); sigma > 0 and finite
fields.epoch: a number (days, any one scale) or null; null means no epoch is known and is treated as nonsimultaneous when an allowance is given

refusals.convention-unknown: no convention, or one that is not listed
refusals.kind: kind absent or not one of the two
refusals.no-bandpass: a band-integrated point whose band is not in the map the caller supplied
refusals.vega-offset-missing: a Vega magnitude in a band whose AB-Vega offset the pack does not state
refusals.band-flux-per-wavelength: a band-integrated value in a per-wavelength unit: it has no unique f_nu (the band mean of f_lambda and the band mean of f_nu differ), so the magnitude or the f_nu form is required
refusals.wavelength: a monochromatic point without a positive wavelength
refusals.flux: a flux density that is not positive and finite, or a magnitude that is not finite
refusals.sigma: a sigma that is not positive and finite
refusals.error-too-large: a flux error of 0.5 or more of the flux (the log-flux Gaussian treatment is not valid there)
refusals.too-few-points: fewer than three usable points for a two-parameter blackbody: status 'not-constrained'
refusals.temperature-open: the temperature interval at the primary level reaches a side of the domain 800 K to 50000 K: status 'not-constrained'
refusals.reference-epoch: an allowance was given without a reference epoch

rules.flux: f_nu (Jy) from an AB magnitude is 3631 Jy x 10^(-0.4 m) (the radiation kernel's AB zero point, Oke and Gunn 1983); from a Vega magnitude the same after m_AB = m_Vega + (AB - Vega)_band with the offset of the pack; a flux unit is converted through the registry (radiation kernel convertFlux). The log-flux error is 0.4 ln(10) sigma for a magnitude and sigma / f for a flux
rules.model: a blackbody of temperature T and angular radius theta (radians): monochromatic f_nu = pi theta^2 B_nu(T); band-integrated, the photon-weighted mean f_nu of the pack's band (radiation kernel meanFluxJy) of pi theta^2 B_lambda(T). Never f_nu at the pivot for a band-integrated point
rules.fit: ln f_i = u + g_i(ln T) with u = ln theta^2 and g_i the log of the model per unit theta^2; with weights 1 / sigma_eff,i^2 the scale u is the weighted mean of ln f_i - g_i and is profiled out exactly; chi-square is profiled in ln T on the 1200-node grid and refined by the interpolant; the temperature interval is the set where the profile is within chi2Quantile(level, 1) of the minimum (statistics kernel profileInterval); the covariance of (u, ln T) is (J^T W J)^-1 with J = [1, g_i'] at the minimum
rules.adequacy: p = chi-square survival of the minimum on n - 2 degrees of freedom; the fit is adequate when p >= 0.01; the result also carries the intervals scaled by the reduced chi-square when it exceeds 1 (the convention of js/inference/fit.js)
rules.nonsimultaneity: a point is nonsimultaneous when its epoch is null, or its epoch differs from the stated reference epoch by more than the stated window (days); each such point's log-flux sigma becomes sqrt(sigma^2 + v^2) with v the allowance, a fractional flux amplitude (0.1 means 10 percent); no allowance is given by default, and then the result says 'assumes simultaneous'
rules.range: the fit states the shortest and longest point wavelength it used; the model evaluated at a wavelength outside that range carries extrapolated: true
rules.integral: F_data = the integral of f_lambda between the shortest and longest point wavelength, with a power law between neighbouring points (f_lambda = f1 (lambda / lambda1)^a, a = ln(f2 / f1) / ln(lambda2 / lambda1)); the model tails below and above are the closed forms sigma T^4 theta^2 (15 / pi^4) times the Planck integral from x0 to infinity or from 0 to x0 with x0 = h c / (lambda k T), returned only when asked for, separately, and labelled extrapolated; the luminosity is 4 pi d^2 F; its interval is a lognormal one from the standard deviation of ln F over 200 seeded parametric-bootstrap draws (each perturbs every point by its sigma_eff and refits), combined in quadrature with 2 sigma_d / d when a distance uncertainty is given
rules.interpretation: the temperature is a colour temperature of the points, not an effective temperature; the angular radius and luminosity from a blackbody are those of a blackbody with the fitted colour; no correction for interstellar reddening is made and the result says so; an absolute scale of a spectrum that is not flux calibrated (a fibre spectrum) is not meaningful

verdictFunction.kernel: A when every leg of the three groups passes; B when every conversion leg passes and not every leg of the other two does (the conversions and the band-integrated versus monochromatic distinction stand, and a claim that depends on a failed group does not); C when a conversion leg fails (nothing built on the kernel ships)
verdictFunction.claimable: temperature: every fitLeg passes; luminosity: every fitLeg and every luminosityLeg passes; conversions: every conversionLeg passes
verdictFunction.product: ESTABLISHED only when E1 passes and every row it uses is basis A or B; otherwise NOT ESTABLISHED

consumersRule.synthetic: A labelled synthetic SED view and a survey-depth investigation on synthetic stars are permitted when the kernel verdict is A, or B with the temperature claimable; they say that the star is synthetic.
consumersRule.authenticStar: A pack, a star's SED view and any sentence about a real star's temperature or luminosity require the product verdict ESTABLISHED.
consumersRule.luminosity: Any bolometric luminosity a student sees requires the luminosity claim claimable.
consumersRule.conventions: An upper-depth investigation on conventions and nonsimultaneity requires the conversion legs to pass.
consumersRule.gating: Nothing visible is built before Carl confirms, whatever the verdict.

checks.what: the conversions against closed forms and the cited zero points of the tree: m_AB = 0 is 3631 Jy and m_AB = 5 is 36.31 Jy exactly; f_lambda to f_nu to f_lambda round trips; nu f_nu equals lambda f_lambda; a source flat in f_nu has AB = 0 in every band of the pack; for every band of the pack the Vega magnitude equals the AB magnitude minus the pack's offset; the registry's Jy and mJy differ by 1000

the band-integrated mean f_nu against the closed form on a box band of response 1 between 500 and 700 nm for f_nu = K nu^p: <f_nu> = K c^p (l1^-p - l2^-p) / (p ln(l2 / l1)) for p not 0 and K for p = 0 (the integral of a power law over a box in the photon-weighted mean); and the monochromatic value at the pivot differs from it by the closed-form difference, so a band-integrated point and a monochromatic point at its pivot are not the same number

the model integral: the data-free integral from the shortest to the longest wavelength of the model plus its two tails equals sigma T^4 theta^2 (the Stefan-Boltzmann law of the radiation kernel's constants), for the four temperatures of the stars and bounds 400 nm and 2200 nm

a noise-free synthetic star recovers its temperature, angular radius and blackbody luminosity: the stars cool, sun and hot on the optical-nir, sdss-2mass and with-mir point sets, noise off, the fit run on the kernel's own points; luminosity is 4 pi (theta d)^2 sigma T^4 against the star's truth 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4

the integrated-SED luminosity of noise-free synthetic stars against the exact luminosity: (i) F_data against a fine-grid Simpson integral in ln lambda of the truth model between the same bounds (the chord bias and the band-integrated point placed at its pivot are inside this bound); (ii) F_data plus the model tails against the truth's total sigma T^4 theta^2

the conversions against astropy.units (spectral_density equivalencies, ABmag, Jy) on the same numbers: f_lambda in W/m2/nm and erg/s/cm2/Angstrom to f_nu in Jy at the wavelengths below, and AB magnitudes to Jy

the band-integrated mean f_nu of a blackbody through every band of the pack against an independent implementation (numpy and scipy Simpson on a 0.05 nm refinement of the response, astropy.modeling BlackBody for B_lambda) of the same photon-weighted definition

the blackbody SED fit against an independent fit (scipy.optimize least_squares in (ln theta, ln T) on the oracle's own band integration and astropy BlackBody, and the oracle's own chi-square profile with brentq for the interval ends) on the very points the kernel's generator made, noise on

the integrated flux against an independent implementation: F_data of the points of B3's three cases against the oracle's own power-law chords (arithmetic agreement), and the model tails against scipy.integrate.quad of pi B_lambda

the roadmap's leg (b), a pinned SED fit from a cited independent tool on authentic points: NOT RUN until tests/fixtures/sed/authentic/tool-fit.json arrives (the files requested in SED_GATE.md); the tool's temperature must agree within three combined sigma

coverage of the temperature interval by the profile on a fixed seeded ensemble: the sun on sdss-2mass, noise on, no nonsimultaneity, 300 realisations; the fraction of realisations whose interval contains 5772 K

coverage of the integrated-SED luminosity with model tails (F_data plus tails, 4 pi d^2, the distance known exactly) by the bootstrap interval against the truth 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4: the sun on with-mir, noise on, 150 realisations of 200 bootstrap draws each, levels 0.6827 and 0.95

coverage of the temperature interval with nonsimultaneous points and the widening rule: the sun on sdss-2mass, J H Ks 400 days from the reference, their truth moved by independent factors exp(0.1 e), fitted with allowance 0.1, window 30 days; 300 realisations
REPORTED, not judged: the same realisations as C3 fitted with no allowance, to show what the widening rule changes: the coverage at both levels and the share of realisations the adequacy test flags

an SED of two points returns status 'not-constrained' with code 'too-few-points' and no temperature, whether the points are band-integrated or monochromatic; three points are fitted, with one degree of freedom stated

every refusal by its exact code: a point with no convention and one with an unlisted convention ('convention-unknown'); a band-integrated point whose band is not in the map ('no-bandpass'); a Vega magnitude in a band the map has without an offset ('vega-offset-missing'); a band-integrated value in W/m2/nm ('band-flux-per-wavelength'); a monochromatic point with no wavelength ('wavelength'); a non-positive flux and a non-finite magnitude ('flux'); a zero, negative and NaN sigma ('sigma'); a flux error of 60 percent ('error-too-large'); an allowance without a reference epoch ('reference-epoch'); the fit refuses the whole SED on the first refused point and names its id

a temperature the points cannot fix is not reported: the veryHot star seen only on the Rayleigh-Jeans side (the rayleigh-jeans set, 50 realisations) is 'not-constrained' with code 'temperature-open' in at least 98 percent of them; the control, the same star on sdss-2mass, is constrained in at least 98 percent

a misspecified SED is flagged: the sun with the 1200 K excess on with-mir (100 realisations) is flagged inadequate (p < 0.01) in at least 90 percent; the clean control on with-mir (200 realisations) is flagged in at most 4 percent

no silent extrapolation: the model evaluated inside the fit's range is not extrapolated and outside it (200 nm and 50000 nm for the sun on optical-nir) is extrapolated: true; the integral returns tails: null unless includeModelTails is true, then the tails are present, labelled extrapolated, and the extrapolated fraction equals tails over total; the bounds of the integral are the first and last point wavelengths

the nonsimultaneity rule in closed form: a flagged point's log-flux sigma is sqrt(sigma^2 + v^2) exactly and an unflagged one is unchanged; a point with epoch null is flagged; a point exactly at the window is not flagged and one past it is; with no allowance the result carries 'assumes simultaneous'
